gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the printers' quiet ratings are best-case, mode-dependent figures that aren't comparable with each other: the A1 mini's 'below 48 dB' needs silent mode plus motor noise suppression, the Adventurer 5M Pro is rated 50–55 dB depending on mode, and 3DPrint.com measured the 5M Pro at an average of 68 dB with a 79 dB peak.
standout_why: I compared against itechguides.com, which quotes the A1 mini's '≤48 dB Quiet' listing title without saying a mode is needed and gives no 5M Pro noise figure, and printingxyz.com, which says the 5M Pro enclosure 'reduces noise' with no dB number and calls the Ender-3 V3 SE louder than the A1 mini, also without a number. Tom's Hardware (the cited guide) and its 5M Pro review came back truncated, so I couldn't see their noise content. Rivals partly cover hot parts already: itechguides gives the A1 mini's 300°C hotend and printingxyz says Toybox uses an unheated bed. That limits the temperature row to a supporting role.
decides: It confirms the picks but changes one reason. Enclosed doesn't mean quiet: the 5M Pro's '≤50 dB' (also in our own product name) is its low-noise mode, and 3DPrint.com measured an average of 68 dB with a 79 dB peak. For a printer running in a child's bedroom, the page should say to use the low-noise or silent mode and expect louder bursts. Our 5M Pro product title should drop '≤50 dB' or add 'in low-noise mode'. The temperature row supports Toybox for ages 5–8: its bed is unheated, while the A1 mini has an exposed bed rated up to 80°C and a hotend rated up to 300°C.

findings.label: Rated noise (condition stated)
findings.value: below 48 dB, only with silent mode and active motor noise suppression on
findings.note: Bambu's own pages blocked access (bambulab.com 403; us.store.bambulab.com and wiki.bambulab.com 402), so this is the retailer's copy of Bambu's spec. The page's wording is 'can reduce the noise level of the A1 mini to below 48 dB'. This is a best-case mode figure, not normal-speed printing.

findings.label: Max hotend temperature (exposed)
findings.note: Listed as 'Max. printing temperature'. The printer is open-frame, so the hotend is reachable. itechguides.com also gives 300 °C.

findings.label: Max heated bed temperature (exposed)
findings.note: Listed as 'Max. heating bed temperature'. The bed moves in the open (bed-slinger design). Max power is listed as 150 W.

findings.label: Rated noise (by mode)
findings.value: 50–55 dB depending on the mode selected
findings.note: flashforge.com returned 429 on three tries, so I couldn't open the maker page. A search summary attributed 50 dB to low-noise mode and 55 dB to standard mode, but I couldn't open the page saying so; 3Dnatives gives only the range. Our product title's '≤50 dB' is the best-case mode.

findings.label: Measured noise (3DPrint.com, Orville Wright IV)
findings.value: 68 dB average, 79 dB max, 46 dB min
findings.source_title: Flashforge Adventurer 5M Pro Review: A Compact Powerhouse for 3D Printing | 3DPrint.com
findings.note: Quote: 'I measured an average of 68 decibels with a maximum of 79 and a minimum of 46 decibels.' Published 2024-08-23. The review gives no distance, mode or meter, so this isn't a like-for-like comparison with the rated figure. The average is still 13–18 dB above the 50–55 dB rating.

findings.label: Filtration
findings.value: HEPA filter + activated carbon filter, 'dual air filtration system, inside and outside'
findings.note: The page says the filters block 99% of particles and VOCs. Build volume is listed as 220 × 220 × 220 mm (about 10.6 L; the page wrongly prints '10.65 cm3').

findings.label: Heated bed
findings.note: Toybox's comparison table lists 'No' under heated bed for the Alpha Four; only the LunaLuna has one. Build volume is 75 × 80 × 90 mm (0.54 L, about 1/11 of the A1 mini's 5.83 L). The page has no nozzle temperature.

findings.label: Price (maker store)
findings.value: Pro Saver $199, Pro Mega $239, Starter $249, Deluxe $299 (sale prices)
findings.note: Listed regular prices: $469, $549, $435 and $489. The page gives no filament price or weight; it says one roll makes 'around 500 cat rings'.
